doc.title: Hal Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Chautauqua, New York, September 12, 1997

title: Playing with famous musicians at jazz parties
summary: He met Milt Hinton, Bob Wilber and others through jazz parties with mix-and-match bands.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money

blocks.x: Well gosh, you have a pretty good list of well known names you’ve played with. Milt Hinton and Bob Wilber and all those guys. Was most of that at festivals?

Mostly things like this, like jazz party work and mix and match. There’ll be one person hiring everybody who’ll put together a set of musicians he thinks will work well together; 99% of the time they do. But that’s where I’ve gotten to work with really great players like that. Because you know they travel in their own circles. And if they’re going to need a drummer, they’re going to call someone they’re comfortable with who they work with all the time. But that’s the great advantage for me having played these things, I get to work with them where I probably wouldn’t otherwise if I’ve been half a continent away. You know I’m not in New York where I’m going to see them all the time. So I’m really pleased to have had those chances.
